title: Ginger Soy Chicken Rice Bowls
seoTitle: Ginger Soy Chicken Rice Bowls | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Grilled chicken over rice with steamed broccoli for ten
subtitle: Grilled chicken over rice with steamed broccoli for ten
description: Chicken thighs marinate in ginger-soy, grill until charred, and serve over steamed rice with broccoli and sesame drizzle. Clean flavors, filling portions, fast assembly.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Ginger Soy Chicken Rice Bowls in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.instruction: Whisk soy sauce, ginger, garlic, and honey. Coat chicken thighs and marinate at least 30 minutes in the fridge. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.instruction: Rinse jasmine rice and cook with 5.5 cups water—bring to boil, cover, simmer 18 minutes, rest 5 minutes off heat. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts.

steps.title: Grill the chicken
steps.instruction: Grill thighs over medium-high heat 5–6 minutes per side until charred and internal temp reaches 165°F. Rest and slice. Target oven/smoker temperature: 165°F.

steps.title: Steam the broccoli
steps.instruction: Steam broccoli 4–5 minutes until bright green and tender-crisp. Season lightly with salt. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Ginger Soy Chicken Rice Bowls onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 10 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Assemble bowls
steps.instruction: Portion rice and broccoli into bowls. Top with sliced chicken, drizzle remaining marinade simmered 2 minutes, sesame oil, and sesame seeds.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Ginger Soy Chicken Rice Bowls — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

proTips: Simmer used marinade 3 minutes after chicken comes out—safe glaze for bowls.
Sriracha mayo on the side beats mixing spice into the whole batch.
Swap half broccoli for snap peas if you want more color on the line.
tonightSpread: Bowls with lime wedges and extra soy on the side.
Miso soup cups for crew who want something warm to start.
leftovers: Chop into fried rice with leftover chicken and broccoli.
Wrap in lettuce cups for a lighter second-day lunch.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Bowls line up fast when components are ready. This hits the healthy night brief without tiny portions or weird ingredients nobody recognizes.
mealPrepNotes: Marinate chicken up to 12 hours. Steam broccoli just before service. Keep sauce separate until plating so rice does not get soggy.
